Definition: from a compound of G3844 and a derivative of G58 (meaning to harangue an assembly); an address alongside, i.e. (specially), consolation:--comfort.
BiblicalUsage: Paregoria is comfort, consolation, an address alongside. It appears once, in Colossians 4:11, where Paul says Aristarchus, Mark, and Jesus called Justus have been a comfort unto him in his imprisonment.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a fellow worker's presence is a kind of sermon, and Paul counted three men's comfort as a gift from God in his chains.
